00Summary at a Glance

Read as of the Oct 14 US close: all four names are in a re-assess-after-conditions-are-met zone · Business results are strong, but prices and charts are damaged
Four optical communications stocks fell sharply together in the US market on Oct 14 (Corning −5.2%, Lumentum −9.3%, Ciena −10.2%, Coherent −9.2%, SOX −4.3%, Nasdaq −1.9%). On Oct 12 Lumentum (−9.8%), Ciena (about −10%), Coherent (−7.9%) and Corning (−6.0%) had already fallen, so the drop from the Oct 9 close is Corning −10.1%, Coherent −15.8%, Lumentum −18.8% and Ciena −20.1%. Reports attributed the move to September CPI coming in at 3.7% year over year, on top of AI financing worries ignited by a Broadcom CEO remark on Oct 12 that the bottleneck for AI expansion is "capital, not chips." No company-specific negative for any of the four was found. The numbers remain strong: latest-quarter revenue growth is Lumentum +109%, Ciena +37%, Coherent +34%, and Corning core sales +17% (optical communications segment +32%).
  • Fundamentals. Lumentum reported June-2026 quarter revenue of $1.01bn against next-quarter guidance of $1.225-1.275bn, and its CEO said some lasers are "effectively sold out through early 2029." Coherent posted quarterly revenue of $2.05bn with next-quarter guidance of $2.2-2.4bn. Ciena reported $1.67bn for the quarter, with next-quarter guidance of $1.75bn ±$0.05bn. Corning guided Q3 core sales to $4.9-5.0bn (midpoint below the $5.0bn consensus).
  • Price burden. Estimated P/E for the current fiscal year is 42.8x for Corning (2026E), 41.1x for Lumentum (FY27E), 50.2x for Ciena (FY26E) and 28.0x for Coherent (FY27E); on the following fiscal year it is 32.2x, 24.9x, 30.4x and 18.7x. Coherent is the lowest and Ciena the highest.
  • Timing. All four closed below the 20-day moving average. Corning, Ciena and Coherent closed below the 224-day moving average used in the "Dante" method (Korean stock YouTuber 주식단테) for the first time. Lumentum closed 0.4% below its 60-day average ($899.7) but remains above its 112-day average ($884.4). Ciena closed below the open ($393.58) of its Oct 6 Dante base candle. SOX is −20.3% from its June high.
  • Next checkpoints. TSMC earnings on Oct 15, Corning Q3 on Oct 27 (per a third-party tracking site; not confirmed by the company), FOMC on Oct 28, Lumentum on Nov 5 (company announcement), Coherent on Nov 11 (investing.com estimate), and Ciena Q4 expected in December (date not announced).

01Who Makes What

All four companies sit on the "light-signal path inside and outside AI data centers." Corning sells the glass fiber and connectors that carry light; Lumentum sells the lasers that generate it and optical switches; Coherent sells lasers and the transceivers built from them; Ciena sells optical transport equipment linking data centers and cities.

Fiber, cable, connectorsCorning (GLW). Wiring inside data centers and long-haul fiber cable
Carries light signals
Lasers and optical componentsLumentum (LITE) · Coherent (COHR). Indium phosphide (InP) EML, CW and pump lasers
Module assembly
Optical transceivers and OCSCoherent (800G and 1.6T transceivers), Lumentum (cloud transceivers and optical circuit switches)
Long-distance transport
Optical transport equipmentCiena (CIEN). Coherent optical transport between data centers (DCI)

Is the "AI optical theme" real?

Yes. But "demand exists" and "the current price is reasonable" are separate questions. Here are the numbers.

  • Lumentum: Annual revenue grew from $1.36bn in FY24 to $1.65bn in FY25 and $3.01bn in FY26 (+83% year over year, +121% over two years), and consensus is $6.34bn for FY27 (+110%). Over the same period the 1-year share price gain of +467% ran far ahead of revenue. The $7.2bn GAAP net loss stems from a $7.8bn one-time non-cash loss on converting part of its convertible notes into stock (company explanation).
  • Coherent: The data center and communications segment is 79% of quarterly revenue and grew 59%, but the industrial segment fell 16% to $431M (segment growth rates per secondary reports). Whether a rising transceiver mix could lower margins is raised as an issue, but no specific analyst analysis was found in the material reviewed this time; non-GAAP gross margin is 40.2%, below Lumentum's 50.4%.
  • Ciena: Revenue growth of +37% is the steadiest of the group, but two 10%+ customers make up 41.7% of revenue. After the Sep 3 earnings, which were strong, the stock fell 10.4% that day, and reports said guidance came in only in line with consensus.
  • Corning: Optical communications is about 44% of core sales and grew 32%, but the other segments (glass innovations +1%, automotive +2%, life sciences −15%) have no AI link. Company-wide core sales growth stays at +17%.
  • Easy to overlook: On Oct 9 Lumentum's CEO said it takes "about three years for a new laser plant to reach customers" (TIKR report). Results are strong while supply gives pricing power; whether the current margin structure holds once capacity is added is the next question.

02Earnings and Outlook

Consensus has revenue rising by double digits or more this year and next at all four companies. Lumentum's revenue triples in two years (FY26 $3.01bn to FY28E $9.95bn), Coherent doubles from $7.12bn in FY26 to $14.77bn in FY28E, Ciena goes from $4.77bn in FY25 to $8.40bn in FY27E, and Corning from $15.63bn in 2025 to $23.10bn in 2027. Quarterly trend: who is accelerating

Acceleration is clearest at Lumentum. Its quarterly revenue doubled in a year from $0.48bn (June 2025) to $1.01bn (June 2026), and the next-quarter guidance midpoint is $1.25bn. Coherent went from $1.53bn to $2.05bn (guidance $2.3bn), and Ciena from $1.22bn to $1.67bn (guidance $1.75bn). Corning's Q3 guidance midpoint ($4.95bn) fell short of consensus ($5.0bn), and the stock fell 12.1% on the Jul 28 earnings day (closing basis). What differs from July is that this drop reflects a repricing of whether "this pace keeps turning into profit," not a change in these numbers.

03Where the Four Companies Sit in the AI Data Center Optical Value Chain

Each additional AI server rack adds, in turn, fiber cable linking GPUs, the lasers that drive it, the transceivers that convert signals, and the transport equipment linking data centers. The four companies cover different links in this chain, but their share prices are tied to the same question, whether AI capex continues, and move together.

Upstream demand: hyperscaler capex

Revenue across this chain ultimately comes from data center capital spending. Based on July Q2 earnings, the 2026 capex plans of the four largest US hyperscalers (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta) totaled about $725bn (reported, raised from about $670bn the prior quarter). Meta is at $125-145bn, Alphabet at $180-190bn, and Microsoft at $190bn for calendar 2026 (including $25bn from higher component prices); Amazon's updated figure was not confirmed. Evercore and BofA see the 2027 total exceeding $1 trillion, and Alphabet said 2027 spending would increase "significantly."

What this selloff touched. Numbers are rising, yet all four fell together on Oct 12-14 not because capex plans were cut but because the financing cost and sustainability of that money came into doubt, according to reports. Broadcom's CEO said "the biggest constraint is now capital," and Intel's CEO also cited rising borrowing costs (247wallst). Optical suppliers' revenue is directly tied to hyperscalers' committed spending (a Morningstar analyst's interpretation, single-analyst view, PrimeXBT report), so they react strongly to rate and financing news. With the 10-year yield at 5.19% (intraday high 5.33%), the issue is not total capex but whether its growth rate is sustained.

When supply is tight and when it loosens

  • Lumentum said new laser capacity takes about three years to reach customers, and TIKR reported the capacity effect could ramp in 2029-2030.
  • The company said it has not yet seen the effect of new Chinese InP capacity (earnings call summary).
  • There is not yet data on how pricing and margins change once supply loosens.

Impact of CPO (co-packaged optics)

  • Lumentum put volume shipments of ultra-high-power CPO lasers in 2H 2027 and customer deployment in 2028.
  • It said it received a first order for external light source modules (ELS).
  • No quantitative figures were found in the material reviewed on how transceiver-focused Coherent and Ciena would be affected.

06Is the Price Cheap?

Among the four, Coherent has the lowest price relative to earnings (28.0x current fiscal year, 18.7x next year) and Ciena the highest (50.2x, 30.4x). Lumentum has the fastest earnings growth, so 41.1x this year falls to 24.9x next year, but that holds only if EPS rises from $21.79 now to $36.02 (+65%) the following year. Corning has the slowest earnings growth (+30% range), yet its P/E of 42.8x is similar to Lumentum's.

Conclusion
All four have earnings rated "very good to good" and price and chart rated "stretched to damaged," so the analysis suggests that an approach of re-assessing after conditions are confirmed is reasonable. Price relative to earnings is lowest at Coherent (18.7x next year), and the case for earnings growth and supply shortage is clearest at Lumentum. Ciena, meanwhile, has the highest P/E and closed below the Oct 6 Dante base-candle open, and Corning, with under half of its business tied to AI and a P/E similar to Lumentum's, carries the largest relative burden. If the Oct 14 decline reflects rate and financing news rather than industry conditions, the first checkpoint is whether the Oct 14 lows hold on any rebound from Oct 15.
  • The positives are in confirmed numbers. Lumentum's quarterly revenue of $1.01bn (+109%), Ciena's $1.67bn (+37%), Coherent's $2.05bn (+34%) and Corning's optical communications $2.07bn (+32%) are results, not forecasts. Reports explain that this decline came from CPI and financing variables rather than earnings (stock-specific causes unconfirmed).
  • The negatives are speed and concentration. A 10-20% drop in three sessions, and with high correlation among the four, diversification benefit is small. On Jul 28 (Corning earnings) the four also moved the same way, by 7-12%.
  • Why Coherent's price burden is relatively smaller. Even if next-year EPS came in 30% lower, the close would be at a P/E of 26.8x, and the current-FY P/E of 28.0x is the lowest of the four. Still, the 40.2% gross margin, negative FCF and 102% annual volatility must be weighed.
  • Remaining uncertainty. The durability of hyperscaler capex growth, the timing of supply shortage easing, the pace of the CPO transition and Chinese InP expansion are still assumptions.

Directly calculated figures are labeled "calculated."

How the Dante method was applied. Dante's 112-, 224- and 448-day MAs are shown together with the standard 122-, 244- and 444-day MAs, and the signals Dante cites as evidence of "institutional accumulation" were searched for directly on the daily bars and attached as a checklist for each stock. There are five criteria. ① Base candle (accumulation candle): a bullish candle with volume at least 2x the prior 20-day average and a body of at least 3%. ② Base-candle open support: whether later closes hold that open (Dante treats this open as the institutional average cost and as the breakdown level). ③ Volume drying up after heavy trading: how much the 10-day average volume after the base candle has shrunk relative to the base candle. ④ Time correction below the 224-day MA: whether a "bowl" pattern of two segments (sideways action of 4+ months) exists. ⑤ Suspected breakdown candle: a long bearish candle with 2x+ volume within 15% of the 52-week high. The ▲ markers and dotted lines on the chart show base candles in the last 150 trading days and their opens (orange = still holding, gray = already broken). Because this edition's last bar is the confirmed Oct 14 close, the close-based breakdown test that Dante uses was applied as is. The criteria are quantified from secondary sources summarizing the method, not from Dante's original videos, so they may differ from Dante's own judgment.

What to check when a zone is reached

ItemWhat a pullback could look likeWhat a breakdown looks like
VolumeArrives with volume below the 20-day average (Corning about 7.64M shares, Lumentum about 4.88M, Ciena about 2.98M, Coherent about 7.01M)Breaks the bottom of the zone on volume well above average
RSIDaily RSI falls into the 30s and then rebounds (currently 40.5 / 42.5 / 44.4 / 39.3)Weekly RSI drops below 40, signaling a weakening trend (currently 44.8 / 52.9 / 46.4 / 44.5)
Candle shapeA long lower-wick candle or a long bullish candle inside the zoneCloses below the zone for two or more days in a row
MarketSOX recovers its 60-day MA (about 12,000), Nasdaq stabilizes near its 60-day MA (about 26,400)Further index plunge, such as SOX losing the 61.8% retracement (11,555). Individual support lines break easily during index plunges
Co-movementSome of the four stabilize first and divergeThe four again fall together by 5% or more on the same day (as on Jul 28, Oct 12 and Oct 14)
Limitations of this section. This is general analysis summarizing where chart supports overlap, not investment advice tailored to an individual's situation. The reference is the confirmed Oct 14 close, and later price moves are not reflected. Claims that a moving average touch leads to a rebound with high probability are not verified statistics. All four zones may be reached or not reached before a rebound, or all may be broken. On earnings days a stock can move 10% or more in a day, which weakens the significance of technical zones. Corning has no Naver data, so some values such as market cap and P/B are estimates or "—".
